key_insight: An asymmetrically threaded SQUID (ATS) coupler enables fast entangling gates designed to preserve Kerr-cat qubits’ strong suppression of bit-flip errors.
engineering_relevance: This coupling approach could provide a hardware building block for concatenated cat-qubit architectures without requiring complex pulse shaping.
method: Use an ATS parametric coupler between Kerr-cat qubits.
Engineer unequal photon numbers in control and target modes to suppress non-adiabatic leakage.
Evaluate a bias-preserving CX gate using full circuit-Hamiltonian simulations.
evidence_signal: Simulations report 99.69% CX fidelity at 50 ns without photon loss and, at a 100 kHz single-photon loss rate, a noise bias of 9922—approximately 570 times that of a naive non-bias-preserving CX.
watch_item: The reported results are numerical; experimental performance and robustness to additional hardware imperfections remain to be established.
paper_title: Bias-Preserving Entanglement of Kerr-Cat Qubits with an ATS Coupler
